questions.question: What did God create on the first day according to this chapter?
options: Light and darkness separated as day and night
Land and seas with vegetation
Sun, moon, and stars
Fish and birds
questions.explanation: God said 'Let there be light,' separated light from darkness, and called them day and night (vv. 3-5).

questions.question: How does the chapter describe the earth before God acts?
options: Formless and empty, with darkness over the deep
Fully cultivated with rivers and gardens
Populated by animals and early humans
Covered entirely by water with no land
questions.explanation: Verse 2 describes the earth as formless and empty, with darkness over the surface of the deep.

questions.question: What repeated phrase shows God's evaluation of his creative work?
options: 'And it was good'
'Blessed be the Lord'
'Fear the Lord'
'In the beginning'
questions.explanation: After several creative acts, God sees that what he made is good (e.g., vv. 4, 10, 12).

questions.question: What special status does humanity receive in this chapter?
options: Made in God's image to rule over creation
Given dominion only over plants
Tasked with naming every star
Forbidden from eating any fruit
questions.explanation: God creates humankind in his image and gives them dominion over fish, birds, livestock, and the earth (vv. 26-28).

questions.question: Why does God rest on the seventh day in this chapter?
options: Because he finished the work of creation
Because Adam requested a day of worship
Because the garden needed time to grow
Because angels completed the heavens
questions.explanation: God rests on the seventh day after finishing the work he had been doing (v. 2).

questions.question: What special garden does God plant?
options: Eden, in the east
Zion, on a mountain
Canaan, by the sea
Babel, on a plain
questions.explanation: The Lord God plants a garden in Eden, in the east (v. 8).

questions.question: What command does God give the man regarding the trees?
options: You may eat from any tree except the tree of knowledge of good and evil
You must not eat from any tree until Eve is created
You may only eat from the tree of life
You must fast on every seventh day
questions.explanation: God permits eating from any tree in the garden except the tree of the knowledge of good and evil (v. 17).

questions.question: Why does God create woman?
options: Because it is not good for the man to be alone
Because the serpent asked for a companion
Because Adam failed to name the animals
Because the garden was too large to tend
questions.explanation: God says it is not good for the man to be alone and makes a helper suitable for him (vv. 18, 22).

questions.question: Who first speaks to the woman about eating the forbidden fruit?
options: The serpent
Adam
An angel with a sword
God walking in the garden
questions.explanation: The serpent questions whether God really said they must not eat from any tree (v. 1).

questions.question: What happens immediately after they eat the fruit?
options: Their eyes are opened and they realize they are naked
They are struck dead on the spot
The garden instantly withers
God destroys the serpent with fire
questions.explanation: Both eat, their eyes are opened, and they know they are naked (v. 7).

questions.question: How does Adam respond when God asks if he ate the fruit?
options: He blames the woman God gave him
He confesses fully without excuse
He denies eating anything
He says the serpent forced him
questions.explanation: Adam says, 'The woman you put here with me—she gave me some fruit' (v. 12).

questions.question: What consequence does the serpent receive?
options: It is cursed to crawl and enmity is placed between it and the woman's offspring
It is allowed to speak freely forever
It becomes guardian of the garden
It is transformed into a lion
questions.explanation: The serpent is cursed above all livestock; it will crawl on its belly and hostility is declared with the woman's offspring (vv. 14-15).

questions.question: Why do the Israelites panic at the Red Sea?
options: Pharaoh's army is approaching behind them and the sea is ahead
Moses disappears for forty days
Their food supplies run out completely
Aaron builds a golden calf
questions.explanation: They see the Egyptians marching after them and cry out in fear, trapped between the army and the sea (vv. 10-12).

questions.question: What does Moses tell the people to do?
options: Stand firm and see the deliverance the Lord will bring
Charge immediately into the Egyptian chariots
Return voluntarily to slavery in Egypt
Hide in the mountains for three days
questions.explanation: Moses says, 'Stand firm and you will see the deliverance the Lord will bring you today' (v. 13).

questions.question: How does God divide the sea?
options: A strong east wind blows all night, making a path through the water
Moses strikes the water with his staff once
Angels lift the water into the sky permanently
The sea dries up instantly with no wind
questions.explanation: The Lord drives the sea back with a strong east wind through the night, turning it into dry ground (vv. 21-22).

questions.question: What happens to Pharaoh's army?
options: The waters return and cover the chariots and horsemen
They surrender and join Israel
They turn back before reaching the sea
They capture Moses on the far shore
questions.explanation: When the Egyptians follow into the sea, the waters flow back and cover them (vv. 26-28).
